task: SpamAssassin original-label spam versus ham; separate from Inbox Zero seven-category routing
data_rights: Publicly offered for filter evaluation; copyright remains with original message senders. Do not redistribute raw mail or send it to live mail systems. Not an Apache-2.0 dataset.
preprocessing: Decode MIME text, prefer plain text, strip HTML markup/script/style, use subject and body only, cap combined input at 8192 characters. No routing/spam headers, filenames, addresses from headers or archive names enter features.
grouping: Connected components sharing exact normalized model input, nonempty normalized body, normalized subject with at least three words (Re/Fwd and numeric runs removed), Message-ID/References/In-Reply-To, or the first 80 normalized body words when available. Conflicting-label groups excluded. One deterministic representative per group. This reduces but cannot guarantee elimination of every near duplicate.
split: Separate retrospective experiment planned after the source-holdout failure. Reuse the same deduplicated groups, hash each group ID with salt system1-public-email-representative-v1 modulo 5; 0 assigns evaluation, 1 calibration, 2–4 teaching. Original and later collections can appear in each split; groups never cross splits. Candidate and baseline settings unchanged. One attempt; no test-driven parameter or threshold changes.

baseline.features: identical teaching-only TF-IDF vocabulary and IDF
baseline.conformal: LAC on the same conformal half of calibration, alpha 0.05

timing: One cold decision recorded separately, warm each path on teaching data, five interleaved single-message passes over the fixed evaluation set; median and p95. Includes System1 strict decision and unsigned receipt construction, no signing or storage. No HTTP or LLM timing comparison.
artifacts: Record per-message IDs, labels, predictions, review flags and sets; no email text. Raw archives, prepared lessons and saved skill stay ignored under .system1/public-email.
limitations: Historical 2002–2005 collection; not representative of a modern personal mailbox.
Spam/ham quality does not establish seven-category Inbox Zero quality or authorize mailbox actions.
Later archive additions are a source holdout, not a strict timestamp split.
Classical baseline is local; no claim of an LLM latency comparison.

This experiment was designed after seeing the source-holdout results. It uses independent public labels and group-held-out model evaluation, but is not a new blinded corpus or evidence of robustness to collection shift.
